Subject: Collecting BRL and MXN payments — intermediary bank fees question

Hi Ben / Laura,

We're preparing to send the first monthly payment for our pilot entity in Brazil and a split invoice for Mexico. Payments ops at our side flagged that some banks in the chain are taking intermediary fees and our AP team is unsure whether to net those or ask Redwood to cover them. Two questions: 

1) Can Redwood accept "beneficiary charges" (i.e., deduct correspondent fees) and remit your invoice net, or do you require gross amount with us covering any intermediary fees?
2) For Brazil, does Redwood need a particular Nostro/Vostro tagging on the remittance advice so your finance team can identify the incoming funds and reclaim VAT where applicable?

I've attached the PO and our proposed remittance samples. Trevor from FinPay is copied — he is our payments provider and can work with the banks.

Thanks,
Ana
Ana Silva

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Collecting BRL and MXN payments — intermediary bank fees question

Hi Ana — thanks for flagging. Short answer up front: we prefer gross receipts (i.e., payer covers intermediary bank fees) for BRL and MXN where possible. If your banks insist on beneficiary charges, we can accept net receipts but need a clear fee-breakdown on the remittance advice and a short evidence file to reconcile fee recovery.

Key asks for operations if net:
- Remittance advice must include our invoice reference (INV-4987) and entity tag (Redwood US Entity 002).
- Bank trace (SWIFT UETR / BB trace code) and intermediary bank name(s) + per-leg fee amounts (BRL: typically correspondent + beneficiary bank; MXN: sometimes MX local clearing + international intermediary).
- PDF of the outgoing instruction (bank stub) or a screen capture from your payments provider showing fees.

VAT / tax note:
- For Brazil (BRL): if Globex is paying gross and Redwood receives full BRL, we will pursue VAT recovery where eligible. If payment arrives net, our accounting team will need the fee amounts separated to determine whether we can reclaim any VAT/GST on the fee portion (often not reclaimable).
- For Mexico (MXN): intermediary fees are generally treated as bank service charges. Please confirm whether Globex wants Redwood to issue a gross-up invoice to preserve net-of-fees settlement (we can do this but it changes the invoiced amount and may affect your AP flows).

Operationally I propose two paths:
1) Globex pays gross (preferred) — simplest from a reconciliation and VAT recovery perspective.
2) Globex pays net (if required) — provide per-leg fee breakout and bank stubs; Redwood will log fee amounts and discuss possible partial reimbursement/credit in the next billing cycle for materially large intermediary fees (>USD 50 per transfer).

I'll loop in Laura and Karthik to agree the exact remittance tags and to provide a wire template for Banco do Brasil and for Santander Mexico.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Ana — quick operational notes and pasted example remittance lines you can share with your payments team / bank ops. We already vetted both rails with our treasury.

Banco do Brasil (BRL) suggested remittance fields (preferred):
- Beneficiary: Redwood Inference US LLC
- Beneficiary account (BRL Nostro): 12345678
- Invoice reference: INV-4987 / Redwood Ent-002
- Payment reference: "GLOBEX Nov 2026 INV-4987"
- Originator to Beneficiary Information: Include "Trace: <your bank trace code>"

If the payment is sent net, request the bank to include an itemized fee record e.g.
- Intermediary bank: Itaú International — fee BRL 42.00
- Correspondent: HSBC London — fee USD 15.00 (converted on stub)

MXN (Santander MX) suggested remittance fields:
- Beneficiary: Redwood Inference US LLC
- Beneficiary account (USD rec): 987654321 (we accept MXN credited to USD settlement account)
- Invoice ref: INV-4987
- Payment note: "MXN payment — include full trace and all per-leg fees"

On VAT/gross-up: if Globex prefers us to gross-up, we'll need a short approval email from your tax team confirming they accept the increased invoice total. That helps our billing team create a one-off gross-up credit note if needed.

Action items: 
- Ana / Trevor: please confirm whether Globex can instruct their bank to pay gross for both BRL and MXN. If not, send one example bank stub for each currency so we can validate fee lines for reimbursement eligibility.
- Karthik: can you prepare an internal playbook for Finance to log net receipts and the threshold logic for credits (>USD 50 or cumulative >USD 100 per month)?

Thanks — I'll attach the MXN example sheet for their payments team.

Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
